title: Sticky session hedger and retroactive crediting orchestrator
creator: Noah Patel
description: Problem: late-arriving events and long-lived sticky sessions currently cause overcharges or noisy retroactive adjustments for customers. This ticket implements an orchestrator that hedges estimated cost for sticky sessions at ingestion and performs bounded retroactive crediting when late tokens arrive. Goals: reduce noisy invoice adjustments, maintain sub-2s read latency for usage view, and keep end-to-end idempotency for replayed events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New hedging metadata emitted at ingest for 99% of sticky session events; 2) Retro crediting job produces deterministic adjustments with a confidence score and does not regress invoice totals by more than 0.1% in the test cohort; 3) End-to-end integration tests for idempotency and out-of-order arrivals pass in staging; 4) Dashboard shows hedged vs reconciled deltas per tenant.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight hedger runs in the streaming ingress (Kafka consumer) and annotates usage events with session_stability_score and provisional_cost fields. A downstream Flink job consolidates per-session windows and writes hedged records to the usage-ledger topic. A separate compacting crediting service (periodic job) reconciles hedged estimates with final events using watermark-aware joins and emits credit transactions to the billing-sink. Key choices: use Kafka for durable offsets, Flink for low-latency windowing, and ClickHouse for rollup analytics. To avoid double-crediting we introduce a monotonic reconciliation token (recon_token) persisted in Spanner; reconciliation is idempotent keyed by recon_token + tenant_id.
design_tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Stream vs Batch: streaming hedging reduces visible spikes but adds complexity to the ingestion path. We accept additional complexity because customer invoice variance is a priority.
- Storage: Spanner chosen for strong consistency at the cost of higher write latency; we mitigate by batching recon_token writes.
- Accuracy: Hedging uses a light ML model (session TTL, request rate) and will under/over-estimate; risk is mitigated by bounding provisional_cost (max 30% of final estimate) and requiring explicit reconciliation windows.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Initial scoping and spike. Confirmed metrics to track: hedged_tokens_count, credit_volume, invoice_delta_cohort.
2025-02-21: Prototype hedger inserted into ingestion consumer; emitted provisional_cost field to test topic (kafka://usage.provisional).
2025-02-25: Flink window consolidation job skeleton implemented; local end-to-end test with synthetic late events shows idempotent credit path working for single-tenant flows.
2025-03-01: Design review with Billing PM and Legal. Agreed on audit trail requirements and per-credit justification metadata. Added recon_token persistence to Spanner.
2025-03-04: Load test planned for 2025-03-07 to validate Spanner write latency under multi-tenant churn.
reviews_and_feedback: PM review (Zara Lee): emphasize user-visible transparency; add dashboard drilldowns for prepaid vs hedged adjustments.
Security review (K. Huang): no PII in hedging metadata; confirmed encryption in transit and at rest.
Infra review (A. Singh): prefer batching recon_token writes to reduce Spanner QPS; suggested 1s coalescing window.
Design review (E. Park): flagged potential edge case where session fingerprints rotate; recommended fingerprint canonicalization step.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag hedger to 5% of tenants and monitor hedged_volume and invoice_delta; 2) If metrics stable for 72h, ramp to 25% and run reconciliation in parallel (shadow credits); 3) At 25% success, enable credits for live billing and ramp to 100% over one week. Rollback triggers: >0.5% unexpected invoice regression, credit pipeline errors >0.1% of events.
